newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Death toll at least 30 in Nigerian clashes.
newsitem.headline: Death toll at least 30 in Nigerian clashes.

text.p: The death toll has risen to at least 30 after three days of fighting between two communities in the ancient southwest Nigerian city of Ife, newspapers reported on Tuesday.
"Arson and looting persisted on Monday despite the dusk to dawn curfew imposed on the town, as partly burned bodies littered the streets," said the majority state-owned Daily Times.
Other newspapers said thousands of residents had fled to nearby areas with whatever belongings they could carry, leaving the streets to combatants and looters.
Fighting erupted at the weekend between Ife and Modakeke communities armed with shotguns, cutlasses and clubs, over the relocation of a local government headquarters.
The Daily Times said over 1,000 paramilitary police had been sent to Ife to restore order, while local traditional rulers were told by the military authorities to bring their people under control.

Ife is the seat of the Ooni of Ife, seen by many of the Yoruba people who dominate southwestern Nigeria as their king. According to local legend it is the first city in the universe, although historians say it was founded early this millennium.
Scores of people died earlier this year in midwestern Nigeria in a clash between Ijaws and Itsekiris over the relocation of another local government headquarters.
